title: Preservation of Dover Forest in Ulu Pandan
what_it_is: Preservation of Dover Forest in Ulu Pandan

sections.label: Dover Forest in ward
sections.summary: The speaker says Dover Forest, a 33-hectare forest within his ward, is of particular importance to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of particular importance to me is Dover Forest, which is a 33-hectare forest within my ward.

sections.label: Master Plan 2019 plot ratios
sections.summary: The Master Plan 2019 publicly states the two vacant plots have gross plot ratios of 4.6 and 4.9 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, in the Master Plan 2019, it is publicly stated that those two vacant plots of land have a gross plot ratio of 4.6 and 4.9, respectively.

sections.label: Ghim Moh older flats plot ratio
sections.summary: The older Ghim Moh flats built in 1976 are 45 years old, and blocks 1 to 6 Ghim Moh Road have a gross plot ratio of 2.8.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The older flats in Ghim Moh, which were built in 1976, are 45 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The current gross plot ratio for those blocks – being blocks 1 to 6 Ghim Moh Road – is 2.8.

sections.label: Proposal using under-utilised sites
sections.summary: The speaker offers a detailed planning proposal using vacant plots next to the CC, the old RJC campus site and the field next to the defunct Ghim Moh Primary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am offering a proposal for that "detailed planning" today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I come here with solutions – vacant plots of land next to the CC, using the old RJC campus site and the big field next to the now-defunct Ghim Moh Primary; all of these are under-utilised.

sections.label: Ulu Pandan BTO and SERS plan
sections.summary: The solution uses vacant or under-utilised Ghim Moh plots for BTO flats and a deliberate, phased SERS exercise to rejuvenate Ghim Moh while preserving greenery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am not taking the easy way out by saying "go build in someone else's constituency." The solution I am offering ties in with my longer term aspiration to both develop and rejuvenate Ulu Pandan while preserving greenery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That solution involves using vacant or under-utilised plots of land around Ghim Moh to accommodate new residents in BTO flats, as well as to rejuvenate Ghim Moh through a deliberate and phased SERS exercise.

sections.label: Rail Corridor access points
sections.summary: With NParks, the speaker secured eight access points into the Rail Corridor for Ulu Pandan residents, listing the locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Parallel to this vision of keeping Ulu Pandan as green as we can was our effort, together with NParks, to create as many access points into the Rail Corridor for the residents in Ulu Pandan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, actually we have managed to secure access at eight points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These points are at Holland Green, Greenleaf, Ghim Moh, Ulu Pandan CC, Mount Sinai, Bukit Timah Road, Ewart Park,	Holland Road.

sections.label: Alternative sites for Dover Forest
sections.summary: The speaker says providing alternative sites and solutions is needed to protect Dover Forest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In order to do that, I have to be able to provide alternative sites and alternative solutions to protect Dover Forest.

sections.label: Thinking before irreversible decisions
sections.summary: The speaker tells planners to think long and hard before making irreversible decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What I am trying to get across today to the planners is the need to think long and hard before making irreversible decisions.

sections.label: Ulu Pandan nature and amenity proposals
sections.summary: The speaker lists proposals including a jogging and cycling flyover over Clementi Road and green corridor access for Ulu Pandan residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That eco-system has been adopted and made to become part of the wider shared landscape of Ulu Pandan residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are other proposals obviously, which I may not have time to go into, but these also include how we can bring nature, greenery and greater amenity to our residents living in Farrer Gardens, building a jogging and cycling flyover over Clementi Road to link the Park Connector from Pine Grove Estate to the Sunset Way Estate, and also allowing Ulu Pandan residents in the Sunset Way HDB blocks to access the green corridor behind them that will link to Clementi Forest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope MND will consider these proposals, aspirations, hopes and dreams for Ulu Pandan.

sections.label: Extended public consultation period
sections.summary: HDB will extend the public consultation period by another four weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: HDB will extend the public consultation period for another four weeks.

sections.label: Saving 44 hectares of land
sections.summary: Doing so will save 44 hectares of land, about twice the size of Changi Airport Terminal 4.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Doing so will save 44 hectares of land, which is about twice the size of Changi Airport Terminal 4.

sections.label: Connecting habitats and intensifying greenery
sections.summary: This will better connect habitats in nature reserves and nature parks to gardens and parks, and intensify greenery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This will better connect habitats in nature reserves and nature parks to that in gardens and parks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will intensify greenery and integrate nature into our built environment, for example, through partnering the community to plant one million trees by 2030 and to implement more skyrise greenery in our buildings and infrastructure.

sections.label: HDB public consultation extension
sections.summary: HDB will extend the public consultation period by another four weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: HDB will extend the public consultation period for another four weeks.

sections.label: Greenery and City in Nature
sections.summary: Singapore's greenery results from over 60 years of greening efforts and government decisions safeguarding green spaces, supporting the City in Nature vision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The lush greenery we see today is the result of dedicated and sustained efforts by generations of Singaporeans who have been greening our cities and planting trees year after year, for over 60 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: It is the result of deliberate decisions made by earlier terms of Government who have safeguarded our green spaces even as they developed our urban landscape and built homes for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These decisions have provided the solid foundation in our vision to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, we are committed to act as responsible stewards for Singapore and Singaporeans, for today’s generation and those that come after us, striving to make good use of our limited land, preserving as much of our natural heritage as we can.
